completion_criteria.text: U1-U7 experiments run and recorded in a companion findings doc; each claim marked verified or refuted with evidence, before any step that depends on it
Step 0 shipped: protect-claude-config.sh narrowed to the gate implementation and deny list only, ask converted to deny, confirmed live
Promotion manifest hardened first: hooks and permissions.deny reclassified so absence refuses promotion rather than deleting from live, and undeclared keys are refused instead of freezing
Delivery path restored under Layer 0: GH_TOKEN exported so gh and git authenticate over HTTPS, and an agent pushes a branch and opens a PR with signed commits and no human hands
Layer 1 made operational: the two PreToolUse hooks registered in tracked settings and promoted to the live install, so checkpointing and rm-to-trash can fire at all
Steps 1-2 shipped: deny pruned to D1-D5 only; all ask rules retired and hook ask branches converted to checkpoint-and-allow or block
Steps 3-4 shipped: allow rules enumerate narrow command prefixes plus mcp__* coverage; settings.local.json truncated to reusable prefix rules and accumulation stopped at source
Layer 1 shipped whole: per-worktree temp-index checkpoint using --force, rm-to-trash rewrite, hourly APFS snapshot, and the D2 age-based reaper in the same change
Layer 3 shipped: one PreToolUse gate, P0-P6 in order, allow/block only, fail-open except P1/P2/P5, honoring the D3 local-container carve-out
Layer 4 shipped: append-only tool-call audit log plus a SessionStart heartbeat asserting layers 0 and 1 and the promotion pointer
Layer 0 shipped: sandbox with allowLocalBinding, allowUnsandboxedCommands false and failIfUnavailable true, keeping filesystem containment with working localhost
Steps 8-9 shipped: inert and harmful hooks deleted; logbook plugin fail-closed guard disabled or patched (R6)
R3 rule change landed: the standing --dangerously-skip-permissions prohibition replaced by a rule requiring layers 0, 1 and 4 live first
Release path closed: a staleness heartbeat reports when local main is behind the remote without applying, and a verify verb asserts installed machinery matches its tracked source
Governed unattended launcher: a version-controlled script is the sole entry point, hardcodes the permission mode, and passes through no caller settings, closing the inline-JSON argv channel
One PR per MSP opened through the centralized pr-create tool, each leaving its base branch green

spine.last_session: Disproved the builder diagnosis. Shipped the bytecode fix as 8377436, verified and already live. Found the live config self-destructing on agent spawn from a non-repo actor, and caused five recursive symlinks inside the release with a non-idempotent recreate command.

open_risks.text: Fix the release builder before trusting any promotion receipt — a file tracked in main's tree never reaches the built release, so config verify exits 1 and the rule it ships has never actually been live

Stop runtime bytecode landing inside the promoted release tree — a python hook writes a compiled file into it at promotion time, so verify goes red after every promotion until that path is excluded or the write is prevented
Edit anything under the hooks directory from a scratch worktree — Layer 0 denies writes there, including to its own tests, so a cherry-pick touching them half-applies and leaves the tree dirty
promote.mjs with no --ref exits 0 having done nothing — no install, no refusal, no output, so it reads as success; it left Layer 1 uninstalled across three verification rounds
Never read a piped exit code as a verification receipt — running verify through tail reports tail's status, which showed 0 while verify was actually exiting 1

A sandboxed session cannot promote at all — every path in the live install is write-denied, so the Stop hook's convergence is the only thing that installs a release, and it only ever converges to main

gh's API is unreachable under Layer 0 — TLS verification fails through macOS securityd and SSL_CERT_FILE does not bypass it, so pr-create cannot open a PR from inside the sandbox; a human runs it unsandboxed
gh auth status calling the token invalid is a false diagnosis — it cannot complete TLS to check, so the token is fine; do not re-run gh auth refresh or re-login on account of that message
Commit signing fails under the sandbox — the key is passphrase-protected and ssh-agent is unreachable, and git -c is denied at the gate, so an agent cannot sign; 67495e3 landed unsigned
Rebase feat/layer3-gate and feat/layer4-observability onto main before opening any PR — both sit on a base older than the landed release, and an in-session task list once wrongly marked them rebased
Anything merged that touches the sandbox block goes live IMMEDIATELY — Claude Code honors sandbox settings from the project file, so it needs no promotion and no restart
Never use git stash while sibling agents run — the stack is shared across all worktrees, and one agent popped another's entry mid-session

The deny entry for supabase db reset defeats the ratified local-container carve-out — the agent cannot validate migrations it writes, and the Layer 3 gate already discriminates local from remote, so it must go when c3 runs
Run the full suite at the merge boundary, not just per-branch — three PRs each genuinely green alone reddened the base once composed
Delete the five recursive symlinks inside the live release before anything else — they make the tree infinitely deep and account for five of verify's seven findings
Use ln -sfn, never bare ln -s, when recreating a promoted entry — bare ln -s descends into an existing directory and writes the link inside it instead of replacing it
The process deleting the six promoted entries is not in this repo — every repo-side candidate is eliminated with evidence, so naming it needs fs_usage or opensnoop run as root outside the sandbox
Do not treat spawning an agent as the only trigger — the first incident has no Agent dispatch anywhere in the transcripts, so the deleter also fires on some other event
Do not cite an empty ~/.Trash as evidence for anything — the sandbox returns Operation not permitted for it under macOS privacy control, which some tools report as empty
Treat the old builder diagnosis as disproven — git archive and buildRelease both emit rules/context7.md, so any fix aimed at the archive step is aimed at nothing
buildRelease reuses any release directory that already exists — a drifted release is therefore permanent, because no promotion ever rebuilds it
promote returns unchanged before it ever builds when live already equals main — so a self-healing builder is unreachable in exactly the state that needs it
Commit with --no-gpg-sign inside the sandbox — ssh-agent is unreachable and a plain commit aborts on a passphrase prompt

key_decisions.title: D2 guards the live installed copy, not version-controlled source
The D6 checkpoint runs at the worktree root and requires --force
Allow rules enumerate narrow prefixes; a broad Bash star rule is counterproductive
Layer 0 survives on one key; the default sandbox configuration is unsafe
Oversight-reducing changes wait for direct user confirmation
Default-branch push denies stay, reclassified as delivery contract not catastrophe
Merging to live stays an explicit human act with loud staleness reporting
No deny entry is removed until its replacement exists
HTTPS and GH_TOKEN are the delivery path under Layer 0
The gh token moves from Keychain to file storage so the sandbox can read it
trash-rm registers ahead of the bash gate so the gate judges the rewritten command
main is published only through a pull request, never a direct push
Release-tree drift is prevented at its source, never excused by verify

out_of_scope: Re-running any U1-U7 experiment - all seven are resolved with evidence in the findings doc, and re-running them costs hours and risks tripping the security flags that already fired twice
Pruning the 58 refs left under refs/checkpoint-experiment/ - deleting refs is trivial but reclaiming the roughly 9 MB needs gc --prune, which is guarded under D2 and is a human act
